review_scope: PostgreSQL 18 schema, immutable migration chain and source sentinels, migration runner, public TLS/pooling boundary, effective monitoring privileges, roles, partitions, retention, capacity, bounded disk/connection faults, physical backup, streaming failover, PITR incarnation fencing, RFC3339Nano evidence conversion, OCI and supply raw-artifact identity/digest closure, and complete requirement-evidence traceability

findings.title: Application-owned migration path lacked an independent fail-closed State target
findings.resolution: Added a PostgreSQL-18-only one-shot migration image with exact database confirmation, TLS enforcement, advisory lock, per-migration transaction/history, checksum drift rejection and immutable chain digest.

findings.title: Cross-domain exact identity and generation relationships were incomplete
findings.resolution: Added exact composite foreign keys, monotonic target assignment enforcement, writer gates and negative blackbox oracles across model, firewall, fleet, plugin and statistics facts.

findings.title: Restore had no atomic target/model incarnation rotation fact
findings.resolution: Added isolated append-only recovery events and an atomic rotation function that leaves both writers disabled and creates no effect/statistics side effect; exercised at a named PITR restore point.

findings.title: No production-shaped TLS and transaction-pooling boundary existed
findings.resolution: Pinned PgBouncer 1.25.2 source/checksum, enforced TLS 1.3 mutual verification and SCRAM on both hops, fixed transaction pooling and connection budgets, and rejected plaintext fallback.

findings.title: Catch-all partitions and retention paths lacked legal-hold-aware bounded maintenance
findings.resolution: Converted catch-alls to DEFAULT partitions, added ahead-of-time partition maintenance, legal holds and bounded security-definer retention for Event, rule rollup and plugin-statistics facts.

findings.title: Runtime login, maintenance, backup, monitoring and private schema roles were not sealed
findings.resolution: Provisioned password-free group roles and secret-backed logins, disabled bootstrap login after migration, removed migration cluster privileges and memberships, revoked PUBLIC database access and verified the exact role matrix.

findings.title: No real 4,096-rule capacity, streaming failover or physical PITR workload existed
findings.resolution: Added exact-schema 0/128/1024/4096 rolled-back capacity trials, bounded four-phase soak, verified physical basebackup/WAL archive, async streaming replay, crash promotion and named-point PITR.

findings.title: Monitoring login membership did not make pg_monitor observations effective
findings.resolution: Changed the dedicated monitoring login to INHERIT its no-login monitoring group, asserted that property in runtime role readback, and proved the same physical standby is visible as state=streaming before crash promotion.

findings.title: State completion manifest omitted explicit PostgreSQL design and common Module DoD requirement IDs
findings.resolution: Expanded the manifest to the exact 64-item bounded State requirement set, mapped every item to existing real command evidence with explicit database-only qualification limits, and raised the shared traceability document bound from 32 to 64 without weakening any result semantics.

findings.title: Immutable migration 0001 contains historical bootstrap sentinel words that could mask a live placeholder
findings.resolution: Preserved the already-applied migration byte-for-byte, proved 0014 supersedes its bootstrap incident comment, proved the runner publishes the exact final chain digest before success, and added a fail-closed sentinel scan that allows only the two exact immutable lines while rejecting any new live TODO/FIXME/placeholder/stub token.

findings.title: Final completion summary did not independently bind OCI and supply evidence to the exact run and images
findings.resolution: Added strict public schemas and final-summary revalidation of run identity, exact image IDs/tags, migration-chain identity, command-sidecar source and log digests, three non-empty SBOMs, four zero-finding scan policies, fresh Trivy metadata, and all eight raw artifact digests; negative tests now reject changed logs and scans.

findings.title: Formal soak evidence conversion rejected Go RFC3339Nano timestamps after the workload completed
findings.resolution: Normalized nanosecond RFC3339 fractions to Python's six-digit datetime precision before arithmetic, added nine-digit timestamp regression coverage, and successfully converted and schema-validated the complete 3,600-second raw workload from the failed diagnostic run.
